main_text.p: sint, tibi donare, dicarem. Munus est Leuidensæ crasso filo factum, si me meáque consideres. Sin spectes res à me aliunde mutuò sumptas, & velut in lancem Satyram promiscuè congestas, oculis tuis fortasse non indignum. Illud ita tibi gratum & acceptum sit exopto, ut non displiceat ulli eorum, quos habet bonos & doctos innumerabiles Britannia magna. Fœlix, si sua bona norit: fœlicior, si iisdem bene utatur notis: fœlicissima, si eadem perpetuò ad finem usque Deo bene favente retineat & conservet. Habet illa φιλοσόφους, in omni genere πολιτείας dextros & peritos gubernatores, propè infinitos. Sed præ omnibus & supra omneis eximium θεόφρον Regem serenissimum, potentissimum & doctissimum, ῥητῶρα λόγων, ϖρακτῆρα τῶν ἔργων. Illi à supremo Regum rege fausta omnia ardentissimis votis precamur omnes, qui hîc sumus pij. Omnibus ipsius Maiestati subditis populis sanctam & constantem in vera pietate Euangelica con-

page.notes: Greek words in the text (φιλοσόφους, πολιτείας, θεόφρον, ῥητῶρα, λόγων, ϖρακτῆρα, τῶν ἔργων) are transcribed as best read; the Greek on the scan is small and partly blurred, so accents and some letters are uncertain. The line "sint, tibi donare" begins as a fragment. The "iiij" signature is printed beside an asterisk at the foot and is treated as a signature.
